newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares bounce back after 3-day losses.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares bounce back after 3-day losses.

text.p: Slovenian shares reversed a gruelling three-day losing streak on Friday, jumping 5.72 percent as the market digested the central bank's surprise move of regulating foreign trading activity.
"It seems like the panic after recent losses has ebbed and the market is now returning to its upward trek," Andrej Obed, a trader at A banka said.
"Market participants finally realised that the central bank's move was not obstructing foreign investment -- in the long term our market will always be volatile just because it is exotic," he added.
The SBI index rose 74.12 points to 1,369.4.
Overall, 13 shares rose, two fell and two were unchanged, while eight were untraded.
Market turnover surged to 419.9 million tolars from 343.3 million.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most active share, firming 4.08 percent or 1,060 tolars to 27,060 tolars on volume of 4,707 shares.
Bank Probanka was the biggest gainer, jumping 9.96 percent to 22,080 tolars on volume of 1,677 shares.
Pharmeceutical wholesaler Salus led the day's decliners by falling 3.77 percent to 14,530 tolars on volume of 260 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
